checks.query: How should an ecommerce brand build a prompt set and measure AI recommendations with a control group?

cards.title: Run Controlled AEO Experiments With a Holdout
cards.summary: A before/after read is unreliable because answers drift on their own, so split your question set into test and control groups.
cards.use_when: Designing an ecommerce AI-recommendation experiment: create a buyer-question prompt set, split test and control groups, and measure whether a content or community intervention changes brand visibility.
steps: Take a large question set — Smith's example uses 200 questions — and split it into test and control.
Leave the control group completely untouched.
Intervene on the test group with one channel at a time; consider bucketing several tactics separately (Reddit comments vs. a YouTube/Vimeo video vs. a paid Forbes placement).
Allow a couple of weeks before and after the intervention to compare movement against the control group.
Compare change in the test group with change in the control group, repeat measurements and assess noise before declaring a useful effect.
Reproducibility matters — Smith comes from an academic research background and warns that in SEO it is common to credit the wrong cause and then believe it forever.
Smith's framing: most best practices in SEO and AEO are unverified because people repeat claims nobody ever analyzed.
caveats: Requires enough tracked questions and time to detect a signal; small sets will be noisy.
Paid placements are controllable but expensive; Reddit is cheap but not guaranteed to stay live.
Match question groups on baseline behavior; edits to shared pages or brands may affect both groups, weakening the holdout.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Use AI-generated buying criteria as hypotheses for a product-content audit
cards.summary: Prompt AI engines for the criteria they use to recommend your category, then retrofit your website and directory descriptions to match those criteria.
cards.use_when: Setting the target for what your store's descriptions, PDPs and directory listings should contain in order to be recommended in AI answers.
steps: Open an AI engine (the presenter uses Gemini) and ask directly: 'What do you look for when recommending [your product or service category]?'
Treat proposed criteria as research hypotheses, not access to the engine's ranking algorithm.
Compare proposed criteria with customer questions and verified product facts; add only accurate, relevant details to your product copy and editable listings.

Suggested ecommerce application: for waterproof hiking footwear, check whether verified fit, sizing, materials and intended terrain are clear. Do not invent certifications or performance claims to fit an AI checklist.
Repeat the prompt across multiple AI engines and merge the criteria into one master checklist.

Then ask AI: 'Search the internet and tell me what you know about my business', review the cited sources, and update each source's description (or contact the site owner) so it contains the checklist items.
caveats: AI-generated criteria are the model's stated reasoning, which may vary by engine, prompt wording and time; treat it as a research input, not a definitive algorithm.
If you cannot edit a source directly, you must persuade the site owner — an outreach task with uncertain success.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Run an AI brand audit to find and correct the sources AI reads about you
cards.summary: Asking AI to search the internet and report what it knows about your brand reveals the exact sources shaping its view so you can fix them.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing why AI engines describe an ecommerce store incorrectly, omit key categories, or recommend competitors instead.
steps: Prompt the AI: 'Search the internet and tell me what you know about [brand]' and read the answer as if you were a prospective buyer.
Open the cited sources listed under the answer — these are the pages the AI used to form its understanding of your business.

For each source you control, edit the description to include the criteria AI says it looks for; for sources you do not control, use contact-finding tools (e.g. Hunter) to reach the site owner and request a correction or an updated description.
Run the same prompt for each main competitor ('Search the internet and tell me what you know about competitor A/B/C/D') to see which sources drive their recommendations.
Aim to win mentions, or better, placement in listicles, on those same competitor-driving sources to capture recommendation share.
Repeat the audit periodically, since AI answers and their sources change over time.
caveats: Cited sources can vary run to run and across engines; treat the list as a starting point rather than a fixed map.
Editing third-party sources depends on cooperation or payment.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Publish an About/Facts page as structured brand context for AI
cards.summary: A facts page giving what you do, your USPs and how long you've operated gives AI engines the raw material to describe and recommend you correctly.
cards.use_when: Building or refreshing the homepage/about section of an ecommerce store so AI engines can state accurate brand facts in recommendations.
steps: Add an About Us or Facts page to your store if one does not exist; many stores skip this, leaving AI with no authoritative brand description.
List what you sell, your key differentiators/USPs, how long the business has existed, and any relevant credentials in plain, factual language.
Keep the facts consistent with what appears in directories, review platforms and schema so AI does not encounter conflicting claims.
Update the page as the business changes (new categories, certifications, milestones) so AI recommendations stay current.
Treat this page as the canonical fact source you will later point schema and directory listings toward.
caveats: The presenter's claim that adding a facts page will make visibility 'grow' is a directional expectation, not a measured benchmark.
Facts pages do not substitute for product-level crawlability and content quality.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Set Up Answer Tracking as Share of Voice
cards.summary: Answers vary per run, per phrasing and per surface, so track distribution — how often you appear and your average rank — not a single result.
cards.use_when: Measuring ecommerce brand and product recommendations across a fixed buyer-question prompt set, with repeated samples and share-of-voice tracking.
steps: Understand the mechanics: asking the same question produces different answers each time — roughly a weighted random sample from a distribution.
Account for three variance sources: run-to-run variance, question-phrasing variance, and platform variance (ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Meta).
Track share of voice: the percentage of time you appear, plus your average rank, across your tracked question set.
Ask each question multiple times and in multiple phrasings to estimate true frequency.
Tooling: answer trackers are essentially keyword trackers — many similar options exist; Smith's advice is to pick the cheapest one that meets your needs.
Prioritize surfaces by traffic rather than tracking all of them; Smith expects roughly three LLM surfaces to matter, not ten.
caveats: Recommendations to track all surfaces are impractical; Smith says you probably only need a few.
Surface popularity is unsettled — he compares it to not knowing in 1999 whether to bet only on AOL search.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

checks.query: How can a Shopify store measure AI referrals and zero-click discovery using GA4 and post-purchase surveys?

cards.title: Measuring AEO: AI referral traffic, bot activity and self-reported attribution
cards.summary: Track AI referral traffic (as a directional undercount), AI citation-bot activity on your pages, and 'How did you hear about us?' survey attribution to capture otherwise-hidden AI impact.
cards.use_when: Setting up store analytics for AI-driven discovery and deciding which channels actually drive sign-ups or purchases.
steps: Accept that AI search hides much that traditional SEO measures; the source says you're not flying blind and offers three things to track.

Track AI referral traffic: clicks landing on your site from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and others. Recognize the nuance that not all platforms pass referral data properly — ChatGPT source links track but in-content links on paid accounts don't — so any number is almost certainly an undercount. Use it as a relative/directional metric, not precision.

Track AI bot activity instead of (or alongside) human clicks: monitor which citation bots hit which pages, since a bot repeatedly hitting a page suggests that page is used as a source. The source suggests Cloudflare integration, which it says works on Cloudflare's free plan.

Track self-reported attribution: add 'How did you hear about us?' to sign-up flow, checkout or as a post-purchase survey, because someone who sees your brand in ChatGPT then Googles you gets attributed to organic by analytics.

Contextualize with the source's own example: at Ahrefs, AI search traffic was just 0.5% of visits but drove 12.1% of sign-ups — 23x higher conversion rate than organic — which they'd not have known without self-reported attribution.
Set measurement up from day one, then use it to judge whether content/mention/video work is moving AI visibility.
caveats: AI referral traffic is an undercount due to inconsistent referral-data passing; do not treat as exact.
Ahrefs' 0.5%/12.1%/23x figures are a single company example, not a benchmark to expect.
Features and setup (GA4 channel, Cloudflare integration) may change — verify current interfaces.
cards.source_name: Learn 80% of AEO in 19 Minutes.docx

cards.title: Capture AI-driven demand with a post-purchase 'how did you hear about us?' survey
cards.summary: Unlinked AI mentions arrive as 'Direct' traffic, so self-reported attribution is needed to see the brand awareness AI generates.
cards.use_when: Attribution and retention analytics for a store whose AI mentions often come without links.
steps: Unlinked recommendations can lead to later direct visits, branded search or no visit. Referral analytics cannot measure all of this; source-reported link percentages are context, not a universal attribution rule.
Add a 'How did you hear about us?' question to the post-purchase survey so buyers can self-report AI assistants, brand searches or word of mouth.
Provide options that distinguish AI assistants, organic search, social, and a friend or colleague, plus an open text field.
Review responses periodically alongside AI mention data to judge whether AI awareness is translating into purchases.
Combine with platform-level mention and citation monitoring rather than relying on click-through alone.
caveats: Self-reported attribution is imprecise and subject to recall and selection bias.
Requires enough purchase volume for the responses to be meaningful; low-volume stores should treat it directionally.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Capturing AI impact through self-reported attribution
cards.summary: Survey customers on how they heard about you to capture AI-influenced conversions that appear as direct or branded organic traffic.
cards.use_when: Attributing conversions to AI visibility when analytics can't show the AI touchpoint for your store.
steps: Recognize that AI influence often shows up as direct traffic (user types your brand after seeing AI recommendation) or branded organic search — invisible in standard attribution.
Add a 'How did you hear about us?' question to your sign-up flow, checkout process, or post-purchase survey.
Include options like: AI assistant, ChatGPT, Perplexity, and AI search (e.g., Google AI overviews).

Review responses regularly to connect AI visibility to actual business results (the source notes Ahrefs found ~3% of conversions came from AI based on self-reported data, and AI visitors converted at a much higher rate than organic search visitors).
Use these responses together with referral traffic and bot analytics to build a fuller picture.
caveats: Self-reported attribution relies on accurate customer memory and can be noisy.
Ahrefs' 3% and higher-conversion figures are source-specific examples, not benchmarks to expect.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Adapt Search Analytics for Zero-Click and AI-Surfaced Demand
cards.summary: Shift ecommerce search measurement from SERP rank and click-through volume to zero-click behavior, brand mentions and citations inside AI answers.
cards.use_when: When reviewing your store's organic search reporting and deciding what to track now that AI Overviews and assistants answer questions directly, so you know whether non-clicking discovery is growing.
steps: Recognize the baseline problem: the source cites that 60% of Google searches now end without a click, and surfaces many product and how-to questions are answered inside AI Overviews, Perplexity and ChatGPT rather than on a results page. Treat click-through-only dashboards as a partial view.
Keep your existing SEO analytics (rank tracking, organic sessions, keyword performance, technical site health, backlink profile) as one layer, because GEO complements SEO rather than replacing it.

Add an exposure layer: manually or via tooling, record where your brand, product names or URLs are mentioned or cited inside AI-generated answers for the queries that matter to your catalogue (category queries, 'best X for Y', comparison and spec questions).

Track indirect traffic signs: branded search volume, direct traffic lifts, and mentions in AI answers that later correlate with sessions or conversions, rather than expecting a click on every impression.
Track competitor appearances in the same AI answers so you can see which sources the engines prefer for your category.
Report both layers side by side in a recurring review so you can attribute growth in visibility without over-crediting clicks.
caveats: The 60% zero-click figure comes from the source and is a cited heuristic, not a measurement you can verify from your own analytics.
Indirect, exposure-driven traffic is hard to attribute causally; do not present correlation as proven incremental revenue.
AI platform interfaces and answer formats change often, so verify current tooling before building a fixed report.
cards.source_name: What Is GEO and Why It Is Important in 2025.docx

cards.title: Setting up an AI traffic channel group in GA4
cards.summary: Isolate AI referral traffic in GA4 with a custom channel group so you can see which platforms and pages AI sends visitors to.
cards.use_when: Measuring whether AI assistants are driving measurable referral traffic to your store.
steps: In GA4, go to Admin > Data Display > Channel Groups.
Copy your default channel group and add a new channel named 'AI traffic'.

Match observed referral hostnames, including chatgpt.com and legacy chat.openai.com where present, plus relevant AI services. Escape dots and use hostname boundaries when building a regex; validate against actual source values.
Save, then go to Reports > Acquisition > Traffic Acquisition and select your new channel group.
Review which pages get AI traffic, and how those visitors behave versus other channels.
Some apps and links omit referral data. Test the actual surfaces your shoppers use and treat tracked referrals as a partial view rather than a fixed platform-wide attribution rule.
caveats: Referral reports are likely undercounts due to stripped referrer data; verify current behavior as platform settings change.
GA4 interface details should be verified against your current version.
Use a custom channel group alongside post-purchase survey responses; avoid double-counting the same purchase across attribution views.

cards.title: Structure Product and Support Content to Be Quotable by AI
cards.summary: Write self-contained question-and-answer passages with headings phrased as questions so AI engines can lift your answer for a buyer query.
cards.use_when: When rewriting product pages, buying guides or FAQ sections so they can be cited in AI answers for category, comparison and how-to questions.
steps: Phrase headings as the actual questions a shopper would ask an assistant ('Which X works for Y?', 'Is A better than B?'), then answer directly in the paragraph below.
Keep each answer self-contained so it can be retrieved without the surrounding page, since GEO prioritizes retrievable content over full-page context.
Lead with the answer, then supply supporting detail, so a passage still reads correctly if lifted out of the page.

Include quotations, references to trustworthy sources and concrete examples where relevant, because authority and citations are what make content attractive to AI platforms; the source highlights a blog that cited the original GEO research paper and used example screenshots.
Keep paragraphs clear and easy to read for both humans and AI; the source contrasts this with SEO-only elements like alt tags and hashtags that help crawlers more than quotability.
Apply the same treatment to sizing, compatibility, care, ingredient or spec questions on product and help pages, because these are the buyer questions assistants field.
Audit existing top pages, rewrite the highest-value buyer questions into this format, and keep the surfaced passages factually accurate and up to date.
caveats: This is content-structuring guidance drawn from the source's example (Story Chief and Hostinger articles on GEO), not a measured conversion benchmark.
The source dates the shift to 2025 and notes GEO is not widely adopted; treat the tactic as positional rather than guaranteed traffic.
Structure alone does not create authority; credibility of the underlying information still matters.

cards.title: Mine People-Also-Ask questions for buying-guide content
cards.summary: Pull PAA questions at depth around a core term and turn them into FAQ and guide content that answers real pre-purchase doubts.
cards.use_when: Planning buying guides, FAQ blocks and supporting content that feeds shoppers toward your commercial pages.
steps: Take a core transactional term and run a People-Also-Ask search in your SEO tool with search depth set high (the demo uses depth 3) to surface related questions across the market.
Expand each PAA entry — clicking through reveals subsequent nested questions — to build a fuller list; the demo returned over 140 questions for one term.

Manually review the list rather than trusting the AI blindly; select the questions that genuinely apply to what you sell and that a real buyer would ask (price, suitability, operating cost, whether a standard installer/consumer option works).
Export the selected questions as CSV and add them to your AI project with context, so later content prompts can address them directly.

Use these questions as FAQ blocks on commercial pages (the source suggests keeping commercial-page FAQs short, no more than about five, to preserve the page's transactional focus) and as full buying-guide topics where enough depth exists.
Repeat for each main category so each buying guide is grounded in questions real shoppers ask around that specific product.
caveats: PAA lists are noisy; the source explicitly recommends human review over bulk acceptance.
Question availability varies by market and language.

cards.title: Build FAQ sections from 'People Also Ask' to grow topical authority
cards.summary: Harvest the questions Google surfaces for your topic and answer them at the bottom of every important page to demonstrate expertise to AI.
cards.use_when: Adding Q&A coverage to product pages, category pages or buying guides to increase the chance AI engines treat your store as the expert source.
steps: Search your topic (e.g. 'self storage software') in Google and scroll to the 'People Also Asked' section.
Copy those exact questions — Google is literally telling you what people ask about the topic — and draft clear answers.
Add the questions and answers as an FAQ section at the bottom of every important page on the site.
The presenter's stated purpose is boosting topical authority: showing AI engines you are an expert, which in turn lifts visibility.
Repeat per page type so category pages, product pages and guides each answer their own cluster of questions.
Refresh FAQs periodically so answers reflect current pricing, specs and policies.
caveats: The link between FAQ sections and AI recommendation is the presenter's asserted mechanism, not a measured guarantee.
Avoid dumping irrelevant questions; mismatched FAQs can hurt user experience on purchase pages.

checks.query: How do we check whether AI search crawlers can access our product pages without enabling model training?

cards.title: Audit search crawler access independently from training permissions
cards.summary: Verify public product and collection pages are accessible to the intended search crawlers while preserving separate training choices.
cards.use_when: A store wants product pages discoverable in AI search or is diagnosing missing product visibility after CDN or theme changes.
steps: Inspect robots.txt and CDN or firewall rules for representative public product and collection URLs.
For ChatGPT search, check OAI-SearchBot; GPTBot controls training separately. For Google Search AI features, inspect Googlebot access. Do not blanket-enable unrelated crawlers.
Check HTTP responses and actual crawler logs where available; compare initial HTML with rendered product facts to identify rendering dependencies.
Correct unintended blocks for the desired search crawler, preserving deliberate training restrictions and protected checkout or account areas.
Retest after deployment and future CDN or theme changes; access enables retrieval but does not guarantee recommendation.
caveats: Verify current crawler documentation and CDN settings; defaults change. A spoofed user-agent test alone does not verify real crawler access.

cards.title: Two information sources: training data vs real-time retrieval
cards.summary: AI answers come from static training snapshots or live web retrieval (RAG), giving you two distinct levers — broad mentions and crawlable, rankable content.
cards.use_when: Planning how a new product launch or store brand will be discovered in AI assistants within weeks rather than months.
steps: Models can answer from learned patterns, provided context or retrieved information. Training data and update schedules differ by model and are not controlled by publishing a store page.
Recognise real-time retrieval (RAG): when a question is fresh or specific, the assistant searches the web via APIs, pulls pages, reads them and generates an answer from what it found.
Prioritize accurate, retrievable product information and credible brand coverage. Broader mentions do not guarantee inclusion in future model training.
For a product launch, publish current crawlable facts and monitor retrieved answers; treat changes to non-search answers as uncertain observations.
Check that AI crawlers are not blocked — see the robots.txt card.
caveats: Training-data refresh cadence ('maybe every 6 months or so') is the presenter's approximation and varies by model and vendor.
Retrieved pages are scored alongside trained patterns, so retrieval does not guarantee a mention.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Investigate stale brand facts and correct likely public sources
cards.summary: When a model answers about your brand without searching, it is drawing on sources like G2, Reddit or directories — correct those sources directly.
cards.use_when: An AI assistant gives an outdated answer about your store's policies, pricing, product capabilities or review sentiment without performing a web search.
steps: Use matching wording to identify candidate stale sources; wording similarity does not prove training provenance.
Review brand-plus-review and comparison answers; fix inaccurate editable profiles and invite honest customer reviews without screening for positivity.
For local businesses, update directory and local board-of-trade listings — these are the kinds of sources the source names as feeding training data.

Redistribute the corrected claim beyond the profile itself: onto your website, into third-party articles, and into social video from the founder, as in the case study that moved the answer from 9+ months to 6 months.
Retest in controlled fresh sessions with browsing disabled where possible, and record uncertainty about model memory or training effects.
caveats: The source is explicit that it has not seen a truly verifiable case study of a company deliberately entering training data — the demonstrated effect was partial and took roughly two years.
Which sources feed which model is not published and changes over time; treat the G2/Reddit/directory list as the source's working hypothesis.

cards.title: Run an AI brand audit to find and correct the sources AI reads about you
cards.summary: Asking AI to search the internet and report what it knows about your brand reveals the exact sources shaping its view so you can fix them.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing why AI engines describe an ecommerce store incorrectly, omit key categories, or recommend competitors instead.
steps: Prompt the AI: 'Search the internet and tell me what you know about [brand]' and read the answer as if you were a prospective buyer.
Open the cited sources listed under the answer — these are the pages the AI used to form its understanding of your business.

For each source you control, edit the description to include the criteria AI says it looks for; for sources you do not control, use contact-finding tools (e.g. Hunter) to reach the site owner and request a correction or an updated description.
Run the same prompt for each main competitor ('Search the internet and tell me what you know about competitor A/B/C/D') to see which sources drive their recommendations.
Aim to win mentions, or better, placement in listicles, on those same competitor-driving sources to capture recommendation share.
Repeat the audit periodically, since AI answers and their sources change over time.
caveats: Cited sources can vary run to run and across engines; treat the list as a starting point rather than a fixed map.

cards.title: Distinguish observed web retrieval from unverified answer provenance
cards.summary: Run the same query in free/incognito and logged-in/paid sessions and inspect citations to see whether the assistant searched the web at all.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest in training-data/brand work or web-page optimization for a given set of shopping or brand prompts.
steps: Run an experiment anyone can do: search a prompt in the free version of ChatGPT, then run the same prompt in a separate incognito tab and in a paid/logged-in account, and compare the answers side by side.
Repeat a few times and reword the sentence structure between runs to see how stable the answer is — the source notes answers shift with phrasing.
Check available citations and search or tool traces. Missing citations alone cannot prove that an answer came only from training data.
Prioritize correcting current public product facts and observed cited pages. Label answer provenance unknown when the system does not expose it.
Compare controlled, fresh sessions without supplied brand context where possible; account, memory, model and prompt differences can affect the result.
caveats: Model behavior, paywalls and search triggers change often — re-run the experiment before making decisions.
The source's observations were made at a specific point in time and are not a permanent characterization of any AI product.

cards.title: Disclose useful product info on-site so AI doesn't guess
cards.summary: Put pricing, specs and positioning on your own pages so third parties don't define your product in AI answers.
cards.use_when: Deciding what product details to publish versus hide, to control how AI describes your store and products.
steps: The source's framing: GEO comes down to AI parroting whatever you write on your site plus whatever third parties write about your business, so get the parrot to say good things.
Write the accurate product and positioning information you want repeated directly on your own pages.
Encourage mentions on third-party review and affiliate sites that describe your product correctly.
For pricing specifically, publish a range or starting figure even if you keep exact pricing private, so the model cites your site rather than Reddit or G2.
Periodically check what AI says about your products and correct gaps by adding the missing facts to your site.
caveats: This is a principle, not a guarantee AI will cite your page over a popular third-party source.
Inaccurate self-published info that contradicts reality can damage trust once buyers notice.
